- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.12) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- If model shows sharp upward spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days) followed by true price drop, apply “overshoot correction” — reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 7–14 days.  
- If true price declines sharply after model peak, assume mean reversion — adjust forecast downward by 2–5% for next 3–7 days, especially if sentiment turns negative.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.16) and model is still rising, reduce forecast by 2–5% to avoid “sentiment lag” bias.  
- For 30-day horizon, if model consistently overestimates by 2–4% over 3–5 prior days, apply “mean reversion bias” — subtract 1–2% from forecast for next 10 days.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated short-term volatility (e.g., alternating +0.12 and -0.11), model tends to overfit — reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 7 days to dampen noise.
